title: Noetive MCP client manifest
description: Declares how each supported editor stores MCP server configuration. Adding an editor whose config is a JSON object of servers keyed by name requires an entry here and no new code.

serverName.description: The key this installer writes under. The only key it ever touches.

packageName.description: The npm package editors are told to run. Must match the name published to npm and the commands advertised on noetive.io/mcp.

allOf.description: The file merger writes JSON. An editor whose config is TOML has to be configured through its own CLI, or the merge would replace a working config with a JSON document the editor cannot read.

configFormat.description: jsonc files are edited with a comment-preserving parser so a user's notes survive the write. toml is documentation only: no file of that format is ever written here.

topLevelKey.description: The object that holds servers keyed by name. Copilot uses servers; everything else uses mcpServers.

install.description: cli-delegate defers to the editor's own CLI, which is correct when the editor owns config layout the file does not fully describe.

expandsVariables.description: Whether the editor expands ${VAR} in the env block. When false the API key cannot be written as a passthrough.

detect.description: Paths whose existence indicates the editor is installed. Any one is enough.

entryExtras.description: Client-specific keys merged into the server entry, such as Copilot's type or Kiro's autoApprove.

args.description: ${scope}, ${serverName} and ${packageName} are substituted. ${env} is spliced, expanding to one envArg flag and one NAME=value pair per entry the server needs, and to nothing when there are none.

statusArgs.description: Args that exit zero when the server is already configured. Only consulted where fallback is none, since everywhere else the file is the better answer.

envArg.description: The flag this CLI takes one NAME=value pair after. Without it, ${env} expands to nothing and the server is configured with no environment.

fallback.description: What to do when the command is not on PATH. none is required for any editor whose config this installer cannot write itself.

path.description: Supports a leading ~ for the home directory and ${workspace} for the current directory.
